summary: Sync must delete activity occurrences inside the fetched window that it did not see, not only upsert the ones it did. Because that deletes user-visible rows, it runs only when the run is a complete account of the window: union seen-keys across every profile, both activities and calendar_events synced cleanly, and no --max-pages truncation.
reason: Upsert-only mirroring leaves a row behind forever when an activity is deleted, moved to another day, or dropped from a recurrence, and every offline read (agenda, feed, backup, capacity, overlaps, drift) then reports a plan the user no longer has. There was no other cure: --full re-fetches but never deletes, so the only way to clear a stale row was deleting the database file. Three properties of this schema force the implementation and must survive a regen. (1) The occurrence date is recoverable ONLY by parsing the storage key: the activities table has a `date` column but nothing populates it, because the day comes from the response map key rather than any field of the activity JSON. (2) Victim selection and key comparison must happen in Go and deletes must be issued by integer rowid, because occurrence keys embed a NUL and SQLite's string functions stop at the first one. (3) Externally-imported calendar events are written into the SAME activities table by a different endpoint behind a different selector, so pruning after an activities-only sync would delete every imported event. The store's ReconcilePartition cannot be reused: it compares BareResourceID, which strips the occurrence suffix, so all occurrences of one activity collapse to one identity.
validated_outcome: Unit tests cover occurrence-level granularity (two occurrences of one activity, only the unseen one deleted), window bounds (an occurrence outside [from,to] is never a victim), the generic resources mirror that backs backup and export being swept alongside the typed table, and each guard in canPruneOccurrences. An empty seen-set is treated as no evidence and deletes nothing, so a run that recorded nothing cannot erase the mirror. Pruning failure is reported on stderr and never fails the sync, because the records written are still correct.
